title: Shared Variable Writing in Read-Mostly Loops (Cacheline Ping-Pong)
pattern: Multiple threads frequently writing to a shared counter or status variable.
why_bad: Triggers cacheline bouncing as CPUs constantly invalidate each other's cache lines via the coherence protocol, wasting hundreds of bus cycles on invalidation messages.
detection: Writing to non-thread-local shared memory locations inside highly frequent concurrent loops.
counterexample: The write is highly sporadic or occurs only on initialization. `Contextual`.
fix: Split the shared variable into thread-local structures or per-CPU counters, aggregating them only when reading.
source: *Herlihy - Art of Multiprocessor Programming*, Appendix B (p. 476 / p. 138-139) and *1701.00854v6.pdf*, Chapter 3 (p. 25).
